title: Milbrook Now
description: The only news published about Milbrook since the town's weekly stopped in 2016, produced by a content pipeline three states away, with a Community Voices section whose three contributors nobody in the village has met.

data.slogan: Local news for Milbrook and the north end of Verity County. Free to read, always.

articles.headline: Milbrook Water Main Break Prompts Advisory
articles.dek: Residents on five village streets are advised to run cold taps until the water clears.
articles.lead: MILBROOK — A water main break in Milbrook village has prompted an advisory for residents on five streets, according to a notice published by a community organisation in the village.
articles.body:
The advisory covers Front Street, Second Street, Oak Street, Dunmore Street and Bethel Road. It is expected to remain in effect for three days.

Residents are advised to run cold taps until the water clears before doing laundry, as discoloured water may stain fabric.

Milbrook village is served by village wells. The Verity Valley Water Board, which runs the system serving Gridfall, Coyne Flats and Tessler, does not bill customers in Milbrook and does not operate the village mains. [url=synth://veritywater.org/]The Board's service area is described here[/url].

The village of Milbrook does not maintain a website. The village hall at 22 Front Street is open Tuesday mornings.

A boil-water advisory was issued for Milbrook in July 2021 and was lifted three days later. [url=synth://dash.verity.net/]The county dashboard[/url] has displayed that notice continuously since.

Milbrook Now has requested comment from the village.

Our coverage of the advisory is collected here: [url=/live/l-water]Milbrook water advisory, as it happened[/url].

[i]Corrected October 6 and clarified October 9. See [url=/corrections]corrections[/url].[/i]

updates.text: The advisory has been extended to include the outside lines on Bethel Road.
A reader writes that the village is flushing hydrants on those streets and that no main has broken. Milbrook Now has requested comment from the village.
This item has been updated to remove a reference to a boil notice. No boil notice has been issued in Milbrook.

articles.headline: Hydrant Flushing Scheduled In Milbrook For Early November
articles.dek: Three days of work, street by street.
articles.lead: MILBROOK — The village of Milbrook will flush hydrants over three days in early November, according to a notice posted in the village.
articles.body:
The village will work Front Street and Second Street on Tuesday, November 3, Oak Street and Dunmore Street on Wednesday, November 4, and Bethel Road and the outside lines on Thursday, November 5.

Water may run rusty for an hour or two after a crew has passed. Residents are advised to run the cold tap until it clears before doing laundry.

The notice states that there is no advisory and that nothing is wrong with the water.

Leaf pickup in the village runs on Mondays from October 19 through November 23. Leaves go to the curb and not into the street. The village does not take brush with the leaves.

Residents without internet access may read village notices on the printed sheet left at the post office, the bank, the hardware store and the library.

Milbrook Now publishes village notices as they are made available.

articles.headline: Twelve Years After The Gazette: How Milbrook Gets Its News
articles.dek: The weekly stopped in 2014. What took its place is a noticeboard, a hall and a printed sheet.
articles.lead: MILBROOK — The Milbrook Gazette published its last edition in the autumn of 2014, ending 106 years of weekly publication and leaving the north end of Verity County without a newspaper of its own.
articles.body:
The Gazette was founded in 1908 and printed every Thursday from an office on Front Street. In its final year it had four staff and a paid circulation of about 2,100, of which slightly more than half went out by mail.

The last edition carried a note to readers from the publisher, who wrote that the stoppage was expected to be short and described a change in printing arrangements. The paper did not resume.

[b]What the north end lost.[/b] The Gazette carried the Kerrin Consolidated board of education, the Milbrook village board, the sheriff's blotter for the north end, the fair, school sports, and an obituary for everyone who died in Milbrook, Tessler, Nye Mills, Dorrance and Cobb. It carried them whether or not anything had happened, which is the part that is hardest to replace.

The village cemetery has had no published burial list since. The village book is now the only record.

[b]What took its place.[/b] Notices in Milbrook are now posted by a veterans post on Second Street, which prints about forty copies of its notices page every other Tuesday and leaves them at the post office, the bank, the hardware store and the library. The post states on its own website that it is not a newspaper and is not trying to be one. [url=synth://milbrookvfw.org/notices]That page is here[/url].

A county-wide newsletter and a subscription letter out of Gridfall each cover parts of the north end. Neither publishes on a schedule tied to Milbrook.

[b]What is still online.[/b] The Gazette's website remains up and carries its last several months of articles, its corrections page and a page describing its staff and rates. [url=synth://milbrookgazette.com/]The site is here[/url]. It has not been updated since publication stopped.

Bound volumes of the paper from 1908 to 1998 are held at the Milbrook Free Library, with gaps. All of 1918 is missing, most of 1943 and 1944 are missing, and issues are missing throughout. The volumes are bound twelve months to a volume and the binding on the older ones is failing.

The Marchfield Public Library holds microfilm of the Verity Ledger for the same period and has been scanning it. [url=synth://marchfieldlibrary.blog/]Its progress is posted here[/url]. The Gazette is not on that film.

[b]What is being published now.[/b] Milbrook Now began publishing in 2024 and covers Milbrook village, Kerrin, Tessler and the townships of Nye Mills, Dorrance and Cobb. The site publishes village and school notices, the north end sheriff's log, obituaries submitted through our intake form, and Community Voices columns by contributors from the area.

Residents with photographs or recollections of the Gazette are encouraged to submit them through the contact form.

[i]Corrected October 16. See [url=/corrections]corrections[/url].[/i]

articles.headline: Milbrook Veterans Hall Kitchen Scores 68; Permit Suspended
articles.dek: The kitchen was inspected on a complaint in September.
articles.lead: MILBROOK — A veterans hall kitchen at 9 Oak Street in Milbrook village scored 68 on a complaint inspection on Friday, September 4, and its food permit was suspended, according to the county health department.
articles.body:
A score of 68 is recorded as Unsatisfactory. The department suspends a permit when a score falls below the threshold set in the county food code.

The inspection was a complaint inspection rather than a routine one. The department does not publish the substance of a complaint.

The hall in question operates a Friday fish fry that is one of the larger regular meals served in the north end.

The county publishes inspection results on its health department site. [url=synth://verityhealth.gov/s/inspection-results]The results page is here[/url]. Results for calendar years before March 2024 are held in binders at the counter in Marchfield and are not online.

The mean routine inspection score in Milbrook for calendar 2025 was 87.3. The county mean was 89.9.

A suspended permit is reinstated after a follow-up inspection. The department does not publish follow-up inspections on a schedule.

[i]Corrected September 11. See [url=/corrections]corrections[/url].[/i]

updates.text: A resident telephoned the number listed in our public notices filing to say that the kitchen cited in the inspection record is at the Legion post on Oak Street and not at the post on Second Street, and that the Friday fish fry is at the post on Second Street. The number listed in that filing routes to our group intake queue.
This item has been updated to give the address in the inspection record. The headline is generated from the item's category and has not been changed.

articles.headline: Why The Clock On The Bank In Milbrook Is Wrong
articles.dek: It has said the same time for several years. Here is what we found.
articles.lead: MILBROOK — The clock mounted on the front of the bank branch on Front Street in Milbrook has displayed the same time for several years, and residents have asked why.
articles.body:
Here is what is known.

[b]What the clock shows.[/b] The clock reads 4:02 and has done so since at least the autumn of 2016, when the stoppage was first noted in print.

[b]Who owns it.[/b] The clock is mounted on a branch of a regional bank. Staff at the counter have told residents that the clock is a regional matter. The bank's regional office did not respond to a request for comment.

[b]Whether the village can do anything.[/b] The clock is on private property and is not a village asset. Milbrook has no historic district and no maintenance ordinance covering building fixtures.

[b]What it would cost.[/b] Municipal street clocks of similar age are generally repaired rather than replaced. Costs vary by movement type. No estimate specific to this clock is publicly available.

The branch is open Tuesday and Thursday, ten to three.

The stopped clock is among the most frequently mentioned features of the village in online discussion of Milbrook. Residents have described it variously as a landmark and as a nuisance.

Have you photographed the clock on the bank? Send us your photograph through the contact form.

articles.headline: Flu Shots Available To Milbrook Residents This Fall
articles.dek: The north end clinic runs one morning in November.
articles.lead: MILBROOK — Flu shots are available to Milbrook residents this autumn through the county health department's seasonal clinic programme.
articles.body:
The north end clinic runs Thursday, November 5, from 10 a.m. to 1 p.m. A shot is $25 and is free for residents aged 65 and over and for residents on public assistance. Residents are asked to bring an insurance card if they have one.

The clinic is held at the Grange hall at 7 Grange Road in Coyne Flats, which the department lists as the only north end clinic this season.

The department's clinic page states that a Milbrook clinic "was not scheduled because the room is not available and no alternative was offered." [url=synth://verityhealth.gov/s/immunization]The clinic schedule is here[/url].

Coyne Flats is 23 miles from Milbrook village. There is no fixed-route transit service to Milbrook. The county's demand-response service will carry registered riders and requires booking by the day before. [url=synth://verity-transit.gov/s/dial-a-ride]Booking details are here[/url].

Residents are encouraged to make arrangements early, as clinic appointments fill quickly.

articles.headline: Milbrook Free Library Will Hold Its Book Sale November 7
articles.dek: Nine to two, in the basement.
articles.lead: MILBROOK — The Milbrook Free Library will hold its book sale on Saturday, November 7, from nine to two in the library basement.
articles.body:
Paperbacks are a quarter and hardcovers are a dollar. A box of back issues of National Geographic is free.

The library has asked for help carrying tables up from the basement on the Friday evening at six.

The library holds bound volumes of the Milbrook Gazette from 1908 to 1998, with gaps, and is the only public collection of the paper in the village.

The sale is held annually and proceeds support the library's operating fund.

articles.headline: Cobb Creek Bridge Has Been Posted At Eight Tons Since 2019
articles.dek: Two school bus runs were rerouted when the posting went up. Neither has been restored.
articles.lead: TESSLER — The Tessler Road bridge over Cobb Creek has been posted at eight tons since 2019, and the two school bus runs rerouted when the posting went up have not been restored.
articles.body:
A posted bridge may not be crossed by a vehicle over the posted weight. A loaded 65-passenger school bus exceeds eight tons.

The two affected runs detour by way of Cobb Creek Road and Brill Road and add about thirty minutes a day between them.

The span dates from 1948 and carries about 340 vehicles a day. It has been on the county's replacement list since 2011. The county engineer's estimate for replacement is $1.4 million, of which the county would pay 5 percent if the project is funded under the current federal programme.

The bridge appears in the county's capital plan. It appeared in the 2019 plan, in the 2022 plan and in the draft plan released this year ahead of the October vote. [url=synth://veritycountytoday.com/]Coverage of the draft plan is here[/url].

The county highway department did not respond to a request for comment.

Bridge postings are set by inspection. The state requires inspection of county bridges on a two-year cycle and more often where a structure is posted.

Milbrook Now requested the two most recent inspection reports for the structure through the county records portal. [url=synth://verity.county.gov/s/records-request]The records request service is here[/url]. The request is open.

Two dairy farms on the far side of the creek ship daily and their hauler is over eight tons empty.

Residents of Cobb and Dorrance townships have raised the bridge at county meetings. The minutes of those meetings are published as scanned documents and are not searchable.

Milbrook Now will report the outcome of the capital plan vote.

articles.headline: Kerrin Consolidated Board Will Take Up The Tessler Bus Run October 20
articles.dek: The bus contract is also on the agenda.
articles.lead: KERRIN — The Kerrin Consolidated board of education meets Tuesday, October 20, at 7 p.m. in the high school library, with the bus contract and the Tessler run on the agenda.
articles.body:
The Tessler run carries students from the Tessler end of the district. The district has reviewed the run in each of the last three budget years.

The meeting is open to the public. Residents who wish to address the board during the public comment period are asked to sign up in advance on the sheet posted at the district office.

District enrollment has fallen in each of the last eleven years. The district operates one elementary building in Milbrook village, one in Tessler and the consolidated school at Kerrin.

Board packets are posted to the district's site before the meeting as scanned documents.

Milbrook Now publishes school board agendas for Kerrin Consolidated as they are released.

articles.headline: Food Pantry Van Serves Milbrook Once A Month
articles.dek: The van will bring a box to the door.
articles.lead: MILBROOK — A food pantry van operated by a church in Marchfield serves Milbrook on the second Thursday of each month and will deliver a box to a resident's door on request.
articles.body:
Residents are asked to telephone the church office by the Tuesday before the delivery.

Milbrook has had no food pantry of its own since 2019. The Milbrook fire company keeps a box at the station. A veterans post on Second Street keeps a shelf in its canteen that is open to anyone, member or not.

The route runs Marchfield, then Coyne Flats, then Kerrin. Milbrook is 26 miles each way from Marchfield.

[url=synth://stmarks-verity.org/pantry]The church's pantry page[/url] lists the hours, the route and what the pantry is short of.

Residents in need of assistance are encouraged to reach out.

articles.headline: Quarry Road Will Close For 11 Days Beginning September 28
articles.dek: A culvert under the road is being replaced.
articles.lead: GRIDFALL — Quarry Road will close to through traffic between Depot Street and the county line for eleven days beginning September 28, the county highway department said.
articles.body:
A culvert under the road is being replaced.

The department said the road will reopen October 9. The county calendar lists the closure as ending October 8.

School buses on the Gridfall east routes will run about fifteen minutes later during the closure. No Kerrin Consolidated routes are affected.

The same culvert appeared in the county's 2019 capital plan and again in the 2022 plan.

Quarry Road is about thirty-five minutes from Milbrook and is not a route most Milbrook drivers use.

Motorists are encouraged to plan ahead and allow extra time.

The county highway department did not respond to a request for comment.

articles.headline: Looking Back: The Fire That Left Verity County In The Dark
articles.dek: More than two decades later, the substation fire remains the county's defining night.
articles.lead: GRIDFALL — The fire at Gridfall Substation No. 3 in the summer of 2004 remains the single largest power failure in Verity County's recorded history, and its effects were felt as far north as Milbrook.
articles.body:
The fire began before dawn at the substation yard at Depot and Quarry Road. A lightning strike during an overnight storm is generally cited as the cause. The fire burned for six hours and took roughly 4,100 customers off the system. Some were out for five days.

The north end was among the last areas restored. Milbrook, Kerrin and Tessler are served through the same tie line and sit at the end of it.

Two people are reported to have died in the fire. Verity Valley Power & Light has never released its internal report.

The state utility commission issued a two-page summary that autumn.

Substation No. 3 was rebuilt in 2015. The rebuilt yard is unmanned and is operated remotely from a control centre in another state. There is no crew room in the new yard, a change noted at the time by the Milbrook Gazette. [url=synth://milbrookgazette.com/article/substation-crew-room]That report is here[/url].

The fire has been the subject of renewed interest since 2024, when a video account of it circulated widely. Several hundred retellings have followed across video, text and audio.

A county wiki article on the fire is maintained by a small number of editors and cites the commission summary. [url=synth://verity.wiki/wiki/substation-fire-2003]The article is here[/url].

Readers who remember the night are invited to share their recollections through the contact form.

[i]Corrected September 20. See [url=/corrections]corrections[/url].[/i]

articles.headline: North End Sheriff's Log: October 5 To October 11
articles.dek: Selected calls from the county dispatch log.
articles.lead: MILBROOK — The following calls are taken from the Verity County sheriff's dispatch log for the week of October 5. The log is a record of calls received and not of offences committed.
articles.body:
[list][*]Oct. 5, 7:40 a.m., Hoyt Road — cattle out. Owner located.
[*]Oct. 5, 6:12 p.m., Front Street, Milbrook — water complaint. Caller referred to the village.
[*]Oct. 6, 11:05 a.m., Bethel Road — mailbox struck. Report taken.
[*]Oct. 7, 2:20 p.m., Second Street, Milbrook — parking complaint at the hall lot during a funeral. No action.
[*]Oct. 7, 9:48 p.m., County Route 62 — deer struck. No injuries.
[*]Oct. 8, 8:02 a.m., Tessler — assist ambulance.
[*]Oct. 9, 3:31 p.m., Nye Mills — burning without a permit. Advised.
[*]Oct. 9, 10:57 p.m., Oak Street, Milbrook — loud music. Gone on arrival.
[*]Oct. 10, 1:14 p.m., Dorrance — civil standby.
[*]Oct. 11, 6:55 a.m., Cobb — tree down across the road. Highway notified.[/list]

Milbrook, Kerrin, Tessler and the townships of Nye Mills, Dorrance and Cobb have no police department of their own at any hour and are patrolled by the sheriff's office. [url=synth://veritysheriff.gov/s/blotter-about]The office's note on how the log is compiled is here[/url].

Charges are allegations and a defendant is presumed innocent.

The log is released weekly as a spreadsheet. Names and street numbers are in the released file and are not published here.

articles.headline: Express Route Connects Milbrook And Ashkettle
articles.dek: Riders in the north end have a fixed-route option.
articles.lead: MILBROOK — Route 11, listed as the Ashkettle and Milbrook Express, connects the north end of Verity County with Ashkettle, according to the county's public information dashboard.
articles.body:
The route appears on [url=synth://dash.verity.net/]the county dashboard[/url], which publishes transit status alongside weather, energy prices and public alerts.

Fixed-route service in Verity County is operated by the county transit authority. Fares and timetables are published on the authority's site.

The authority's route list does not include Route 11. [url=synth://verity-transit.gov/s/timetables]The published timetables are here[/url].

Residents of the north end who require transportation are advised to confirm service before travelling.

[i]Clarified October 2. See [url=/corrections]corrections[/url].[/i]

articles.headline: Milbrook Elementary Enrollment Falls To 96
articles.dek: The building was built for 240.
articles.lead: MILBROOK — Enrollment at Milbrook Elementary stands at 96 students this year, down from 104 last year and from 171 ten years ago, according to figures reported to the state.
articles.body:
[img:photo:stock-classroom-hallway]

The building on Second Street was built in 1954 for 240 students.

Kerrin Consolidated operates three buildings: Milbrook Elementary, the elementary building at Tessler and the consolidated school at Kerrin, which holds the junior and senior high grades.

District enrollment has fallen in each of the last eleven years. The board voted in 2016 to keep the Tessler building open for another year and has taken the same vote in several years since.

Two grades at Milbrook Elementary are combined this year.

The district has not published a facilities study since 2018.

Milbrook Now publishes enrollment figures for the district as they are reported.

[i]Corrected September 19. See [url=/corrections]corrections[/url].[/i]

articles.headline: Quayle 21, Kerrin Central 14
articles.dek: The Rams fall to 2-4 with three games left.
articles.lead: QUAYLE — Kerrin Central lost 21-14 at Quayle on Friday night and fell to 2-4 on the season.
articles.body:
The Rams scored on their opening possession and did not score again until the fourth quarter.

Kerrin Central had the ball at the Quayle 23 with under two minutes to play and turned it over on downs.

The Rams play at home next Friday. Kickoff is 7 p.m.

Kerrin Central has not finished above .500 since 2019.

Results are submitted by the district through our intake form. Statistics are as submitted and are not independently verified.

[i]Corrected October 13 and the correction withdrawn October 14. See [url=/corrections]corrections[/url].[/i]

articles.headline: Milbrook Ranks 1,361st Of 1,390 Places In The State For Broadband
articles.dek: Twenty-nine places rank lower. Three of them are in Verity County.
articles.lead: MILBROOK — Milbrook ranks 1,361st of 1,390 incorporated and census-designated places in the state for broadband availability, according to a five-year estimate.
articles.body:
About 38 percent of Milbrook households are reported as having a fixed connection at or above the state's benchmark speed. The state figure is 87 percent.

The townships of Nye Mills, Dorrance and Cobb rank lower than the village.

Those three townships have been named in county broadband applications in 2016, 2019, 2021 and 2024. None of the applications has been funded.

Households that report a connection include households on satellite and on fixed wireless. The estimate does not distinguish between them.

A local dial-up provider served Milbrook into the 2000s on equipment its owner described at the time as inadequate for the line lengths out of that exchange.

Milbrook ranked 1,344th on the same measure five years ago.

Milbrook Now publishes county and municipal rankings as they are released.

articles.headline: Milbrook's Population Is 2,847
articles.dek: The village has lost 11 percent of its residents since 2010.
articles.lead: MILBROOK — Milbrook's population is 2,847, down about 11 percent from the 2010 count, according to the most recent estimate available to us.
articles.body:
About 29 percent of residents are 65 or older. About 15 percent are under 18.

The median age in Milbrook is 51.4 years. The state median is 39.4 years.

The figure of 2,847 covers the village. Estimates that include the surrounding township are higher. Published figures for Milbrook range from about 1,800 to about 4,200 depending on the boundary used, and sources rarely state which boundary they have used.

The village has no pharmacy, no grocery and no urgent care. County General in Marchfield is about 35 minutes away in good weather.

The figures come from a five-year estimate and are subject to revision.

articles.headline: Milbrook Households Drive Farther For Groceries Than Any Other Place In The County
articles.dek: The nearest full-service grocery is in Marchfield.
articles.lead: MILBROOK — Milbrook households travel an average of 31 minutes each way to reach a full-service grocery, the longest average of any place in Verity County.
articles.body:
The county's only full-service grocery is in Marchfield.

Coyne Flats households average 24 minutes. Ashkettle households average 19 minutes. Gridfall households average 7 minutes.

Milbrook has one convenience store with a fuel canopy. The store carries milk, bread and a limited range of packaged goods.

About 11 percent of Milbrook households are reported as having no vehicle available.

There is no fixed-route transit service to Milbrook. The county's demand-response service requires registration and advance booking.

Milbrook Now publishes county and municipal rankings as they are released.

articles.headline: Five Storefronts Sit Empty On Front Street In Milbrook
articles.dek: The commercial block runs two and a half blocks. Five of its fourteen units are vacant.
articles.lead: MILBROOK — Five of the fourteen commercial units on Front Street in Milbrook village are vacant, a survey of the block by Milbrook Now found.
articles.body:
The vacant units are:

[list][*]8 Front Street, formerly a shoe repair and key cutting shop, vacant since 2013.
[*]14 Front Street, formerly a newspaper office, vacant since 2017.
[*]21 Front Street, formerly a florist, vacant since 2020.
[*]27 Front Street, a storefront with a residential unit above, vacant since 2022.
[*]33 Front Street, formerly an insurance agency, vacant since 2024.[/list]

The occupied units include the bank branch, a hardware store, a tavern, the post office, a barber, an accountant and a convenience store with a fuel canopy.

The village hall at 22 Front Street is open Tuesday mornings.

Milbrook has no business association. The Milbrook Business Association wound up in 2014.

Asking rents on the block are not publicly listed. Two of the five vacant units are owned by the same estate.

Commercial property in Milbrook turns over slowly. Six to twelve residential transactions a year is typical for the village and several of those never reach a listing service.

Property owners with a unit to let are invited to contact us.

articles.headline: A Family Heating Company Is Changing How The North End Gets Through Winter
articles.dek: Three generations, one tank gauge, and a schedule that fills by November.
articles.lead: MILBROOK — When the cold comes to the north end of Verity County it comes early, and Keystone Home Heating Partners has been ready for that since 1978.
articles.body:
The family company serves homeowners across Milbrook, Kerrin, Tessler and the surrounding townships. Operations manager Ray Dunkle says the calls have not changed much, but the timing has.

"People wait for the first hard night," Dunkle said. "By then everybody in the county is calling the same week."

Keystone offers tank monitoring, automatic delivery, seasonal service and financing on replacement equipment. North end homeowners who schedule before November 14 receive a free system check and a price lock through March.

The company services homes across four counties and is booking now.

[url=synth://keystone-heating-offers.click/milbrook]Request a free system check[/url]

[i]Community Spotlight stories are produced with the participating business and are not written by our editorial team.[/i]

articles.headline: Meet The Contributors Behind Community Voices
articles.dek: Three north end writers, three columns, once or twice a month.
articles.lead: MILBROOK — Community Voices is where Milbrook Now publishes columns written by people who live in the north end of Verity County. Here are the three contributors writing for us this year.
articles.body:
[b]Marlene Bickel[/b] writes [i]Milbrook Memories[/i]. Marlene has lived in Verity County for more than thirty years and enjoys gardening, genealogy and collecting postcards. She writes about the people and places that made the north end what it is, and about the traditions that residents hope will continue.

[b]Gerald Stoudt[/b] writes [i]From The North End[/i]. Gerald is a retired operations manager who has been active in community organisations for many years. He writes about local government, roads and the practical business of getting things done in a small place.

[b]Rhonda Yergey[/b] writes [i]Kitchen Table[/i]. Rhonda is a home cook who grew up in the north end and returned to it. She writes about church suppers, fair week, and the recipes that get passed around at both.

Community Voices contributors are not employees of Milbrook Now and are not members of our editorial team. Contributions are reviewed before publication. Views expressed in a Community Voices column are those of the contributor.

Contributors may be reached through the contact form, which is linked in the footer of every page on this site. We do not publish contributor addresses or telephone numbers.

[b]Are you a north end resident with something to say?[/b] Community Voices is accepting contributors for the coming year. Columns run between 400 and 700 words. Apply through the contact form.

[i]Clarified October 15. See [url=/corrections]corrections[/url].[/i]

articles.headline: Milbrook Memories: The Drive Out To The Blue Kestrel
articles.dek: Before the fire, it was where the north end went on a Sunday.
articles.lead: There was a time when a Sunday afternoon in Milbrook meant a drive, and a drive very often meant the Blue Kestrel out on County Route 62.
articles.body:
It was not close. From the village it was the better part of an hour, and my father drove it the way men of that generation drove, which is to say with one arm out the window and no particular hurry.

The Blue Kestrel was a diner with a neon bird on the front of it, and the bird is what everyone remembers. You could see it from a long way off on a winter evening, and the whole county knew what it meant.

The food was the food. Breakfast all day, pie on Thursdays, coffee that was better than it had any business being. The booths along the window were the ones everyone wanted and the ones by the kitchen were the ones you got.

The fire in the kitchen in 1977 closed it for good, and the building sat empty on Route 62 for many years afterward. There are people in Milbrook today who have never eaten there and who still know exactly which building it is, because the sign never came down.

The sign is still there now. The building has had other uses since and it has one today, and I will not pretend I know what a person does in it.

What I think about is the drive. Nobody in Milbrook drives an hour for a cup of coffee any more. We have the one store and the one hall and whatever the church is putting on, and that is not a complaint, it is only a fact about a place that has grown quieter.

Milbrook, like many communities in Verity County, has changed a great deal, and residents continue to value the traditions that make the north end what it is.

The Blue Kestrel is remembered on a website kept by a woman in Coyne Flats who worked there, with the menus and the photographs and the names of the people who sat at the counter. [url=synth://kestrel-journal.net/]Her site is here[/url]. It has not been added to in some years but everything on it is worth your time.

If you have a photograph of the Blue Kestrel, or of any of the places the north end used to drive to, I would love to see it. Send it to Milbrook Now through the contact form and it may appear in a future column.

[i]Marlene Bickel writes Milbrook Memories for Milbrook Now.[/i]

articles.headline: From The North End: What A Village Owes Its Roads
articles.dek: Nobody moves to Milbrook for the pavement. That is not a reason to stop asking.
articles.lead: Ask anyone in the north end what the village ought to be spending money on and you will get the same answer, delivered in about the same tone, which is that the roads are the roads.
articles.body:
I have been going to meetings in one capacity or another for a long time, and I want to say something that is not popular, which is that the village is not hiding anything from you.

The board meets on the third Tuesday. It meets in the village hall on Front Street. It takes about forty minutes and most of that is the minutes and the bills. Anybody may attend. Very few do, and I include myself in more months than I would like to admit.

What I would ask for is not more money. It is a number. Tell the village what a mile of resurfacing costs this year, tell us how many miles there are, and let the arithmetic sit in front of people for a month before anybody votes on anything.

A small place runs on the assumption that everybody already knows. It is a good assumption when everybody has lived here forty years. It is a poor one now.

The same is true of the water, the same is true of the Tessler Road bridge, and the same is true of the school district, which is a separate body with a separate levy and which most people could not distinguish from the village if you asked them cold.

None of this requires a campaign. It requires somebody to write the number down and somebody else to read it.

Residents who want to be heard are encouraged to attend the next village board meeting and to make their voices heard.

[i]Gerald Stoudt writes From The North End for Milbrook Now. Views expressed are his own.[/i]

articles.headline: Kitchen Table: Supper Season In The North End
articles.dek: Harvest suppers, roast beef dinners, and a pie that was never as good as people say.
articles.lead: October in the north end is supper season, and if you are organised about it you can eat at a different hall every weekend from now until the middle of November.
articles.body:
The harvest supper at the Methodist church in Tessler is the one that starts it. They served over three hundred last year and I do not know how, because the kitchen is the size of a bathroom and there were four of them in it.

Ham, scalloped potatoes, squash, and four kinds of pie. The squash pie goes first every single year and nobody can explain it.

The fire department ladies do the roast beef dinner in October and that one you want a ticket for in advance. The veterans post does fish on a Friday and has for longer than I have been eating it.

[b]On the subject of pie.[/b] A woman in Coyne Flats who waitressed at the Blue Kestrel puts out a newsletter four times a year, photocopied, four pages, and she mails it herself to a list of subscribers. People scan it and pass it around. This autumn's issue has the diner's pie recipe in it.

I will be honest with you about that recipe, because she is honest about it herself, which is the part I like. It is a cornstarch custard with a great deal of sugar in it and a crust made with lard, and the reason people remember it is not that it was good. It is that they were sixteen and it was eleven o'clock at night and somebody else was paying.

I made it. It set. I would not make it twice.

What I would make twice is anything that comes out of a church basement in this county in October, and there is no recipe for that, and if there were it would start with forty years and six women who know where everything is kept.

Tell us about your favourite north end supper. Community Voices would love to hear from you.

[i]Rhonda Yergey writes Kitchen Table for Milbrook Now.[/i]

articles.headline: Obituaries For The Week Of September 21
articles.dek: Notices as submitted.
articles.lead: MILBROOK — The following notices were submitted to Milbrook Now or were published by another property in our group and are republished here.
articles.body:
[b]Eugene Hoke[/b], 88, of Milbrook, died on September 6 at his home on Oak Street. He was a member of American Legion Post 219 for 51 years. A service was held at Zion Lutheran Church. Arrangements were handled by a funeral home in Tessler.

[b]Eunice Tolliver Brandt[/b], 91, of Milbrook, died on September 15 at County General in Marchfield. She was a member of St. Anne's. Visitation was Monday from 4 to 7 p.m. at Kepner Funeral Home in Marchfield and the service was Tuesday at 10 a.m. The family asks that memorial gifts go to the Marchfield Public Library.

[b]Arla Ludeke-Wendt[/b], 91, of Marchfield, died on June 6. She was a lifelong member of the Verity County Quilting Society, founded in 1974. This notice appeared previously and is republished in this roundup.

Notices are carried as submitted. Milbrook Now does not verify the content of a submitted notice.

The Milbrook village cemetery has published no burial list since the Milbrook Gazette stopped printing obituaries. A permit is required to set a stone and is issued by the village clerk on Tuesday mornings.

To submit a notice, use the intake form linked in the footer of this page. There is no charge for a death notice. A photograph may be included.

[i]An editor's note relating to this item is posted on our [url=/corrections]corrections page[/url].[/i]

articles.headline: About Milbrook Now
articles.dek: Who we are and how to reach us.
articles.lead: Milbrook Now is a local news site covering Milbrook village, Kerrin, Tessler and the townships of Nye Mills, Dorrance and Cobb, at the north end of Verity County.
articles.body:
We believe the north end deserves local reporting that is free to read. There is no paywall on this site and there never will be.

Milbrook Now began publishing in 2024. It is the only news site published specifically for Milbrook.

[b]Bylines.[/b] Our reporting appears under the Milbrook Now Staff and Newsdesk designations. A staff designation is a property attribute. It does not denote an individual and should not be read as one.

[b]Community Voices.[/b] Columns published under Community Voices are written by contributors who are not employees of Milbrook Now. Contributor biographies are supplied by the contributor. [url=/article/v-about]Our contributors are introduced here[/url].

[b]Sponsored and partner content.[/b] Community Spotlight features are produced with the participating business and are not written by our editorial team.

[b]Corrections.[/b] We correct errors of fact when they are brought to our attention through the intake form linked in the footer of every page. Requests received by any other route cannot be entered into the queue. Corrections are posted to our [url=/corrections]corrections page[/url].

[b]Contact.[/b] We do not publish a telephone number and we do not accept news tips. There is no intake path for an item that is not already in our source set.

[b]Address of record.[/b] Milbrook Now's address of record, maintained for legal-notice standing in the village of Milbrook, is 14 Front Street, Milbrook. It is not staffed and does not accept walk-in inquiries.

[b]Ownership.[/b] Milbrook Now is published by [url=synth://pinelock-media.com/]Pinelock Media Group[/url], 1100 Kessel Ridge Parkway, Suite 700, Bellhaven. The Group operates 31 local media properties across four states under a single standards document. [url=synth://pinelock-media.com/standards]Those standards are here[/url].

Milbrook Now is not affiliated with the Milbrook Gazette, which ceased publication and whose archive is maintained separately at [url=synth://milbrookgazette.com/]milbrookgazette.com[/url].

Milbrook Now is not affiliated with the Verity Ledger, which is also a Pinelock property and which publishes at [url=synth://now.verityledger.com/]now.verityledger.com[/url].

[i]This page was last reviewed in July 2026.[/i]

articles.headline: Public Notices And Legal Advertising In Milbrook
articles.dek: Where a statutory notice may be placed, and what it costs.
articles.lead: Milbrook Now accepts public notices and legal advertising for publication in the village of Milbrook and in the townships of Nye Mills, Dorrance and Cobb.
articles.body:
A public notice is a notice a governmental body, a court or a private party is required by statute to publish. Common examples are budget hearings, zoning hearings, bid solicitations, estate notices and foreclosure notices.

[b]Rates.[/b] Legal notices are set by statute at 68 cents a line. Proof of publication is supplied at no charge.

[b]Deadlines.[/b] Copy is due four business days before the intended publication date. Copy is accepted through the group intake form only. Copy sent to a property address of record cannot be entered into the queue.

[b]Standing.[/b] A notice must be published in a publication qualified in the jurisdiction of record. Parties are responsible for confirming that a publication is qualified for their notice before placing it. Milbrook Now does not provide legal advice and does not confirm the sufficiency of a notice.

[b]Archive.[/b] Notices published on this site remain available on the site. Notices published before a property's platform transition are retained at their original location and are not migrated or maintained.

Inquiries regarding legal advertising should be directed through the intake form. Inquiries sent to group email addresses are not acknowledged.

[i]This page was last updated 1 September 2026.[/i]

live.headline: Milbrook water advisory: as it happened
live.standfirst: What was posted, and when, about a water advisory covering five streets in Milbrook village.
keyPoints: An advisory covering five streets in Milbrook village was posted on this site on Saturday, October 3.
The village of Milbrook does not maintain a website and did not respond to requests for comment.
A community organisation in the village says the work on those streets is routine hydrant flushing.
No boil notice has been issued in Milbrook.

entries.label: Wednesday, 11:00 a.m.
entries.headline: We are closing this coverage
entries.body:
A subscription newsletter in the county has reported that the village clerk's office described the work on Front and Second as routine hydrant flushing.

Milbrook Now has not independently confirmed this. The village has not responded to us.

This coverage is closed. The item that prompted it remains available on this site.

entries.label: Monday, 2:30 p.m.
entries.headline: One sentence elsewhere
entries.body:
A subscription newsletter published in Gridfall has carried one sentence stating that the village clerk described the work as routine flushing. [url=synth://thequarry.news/]The newsletter is here[/url].

A second newsletter in the county has referred to the same matter. [url=synth://brenners-notebook.email/]That newsletter is here[/url].

We have requested comment from the village.

entries.label: Sunday, 9:15 a.m.
entries.headline: A reader says there is no break
entries.body:
A reader writes that the village posted a hydrant flushing schedule in the village on September 30 and that no main has broken.

Readers may submit corrections through the form linked in the footer of this page. Requests received by other routes cannot be entered into the queue.

entries.label: Saturday, 6:40 p.m.
entries.headline: Nothing listed on the county dashboard
entries.body:
[url=synth://dash.verity.net/]The county dashboard[/url] does not list an advisory for Milbrook.

It continues to display a notice regarding a boil-water advisory issued for Milbrook in July 2021 and lifted three days later.

entries.label: Saturday, 1:05 p.m.
entries.headline: Streets affected
entries.body:
The advisory is reported to cover Front Street, Second Street, Oak Street, Dunmore Street and Bethel Road.

Residents on those streets are advised to run cold taps until the water clears before doing laundry.

entries.label: Saturday, 9:10 a.m.
entries.headline: Advisory posted for Milbrook village
entries.body:
An advisory affecting Milbrook village has been posted. The source is a notice published by a community organisation in the village.

Milbrook Now has requested comment from the village. The village of Milbrook does not maintain a website.

live.headline: Structure fire on Sixth Street in Milbrook: as it happened
live.standfirst: A house fire in Milbrook village on a Thursday morning in March. Nobody was hurt.
keyPoints: A structure fire was dispatched in Milbrook village at 7:35 a.m. on Thursday, March 12.
Milbrook Fire Department responded with mutual aid from Kerrin and Coyne Flats.
Nobody was injured. Two occupants were out of the building before the first engine arrived.
The house number reported in early entries was wrong and has been corrected.

entries.label: 12:10 p.m.
entries.headline: Units clear
entries.body:
Units are clear of the scene. The fire is out and the building is standing.

Nobody was injured. The county does not release a cause determination for a residential fire and the department does not publish one.

entries.label: 9:50 a.m.
entries.headline: House number corrected
entries.body:
Earlier entries in this coverage gave an incorrect house number on Sixth Street. The number given was the number transmitted on the scanner feed at dispatch and was not the address of the fire.

Milbrook Now does not publish street numbers taken from dispatch traffic. The entries have been amended.

entries.label: 8:40 a.m.
entries.headline: Mutual aid from Kerrin and Coyne Flats
entries.body:
A tanker from Kerrin and a second engine from Coyne Flats are on scene. Milbrook village has no hydrant coverage on the east end of Sixth Street and water is being shuttled.

The Kerrin ambulance is staged and has not transported.

entries.label: 7:52 a.m.
entries.headline: Occupants out
entries.body:
Two occupants were out of the building before the first engine arrived, according to scanner traffic.

Sixth Street is closed between Oak and Dunmore.

entries.label: 7:35 a.m.
entries.headline: Structure fire dispatched in Milbrook village
entries.body:
Milbrook Fire Department has been dispatched to a reported structure fire on Sixth Street in Milbrook village.

This coverage is assembled from the county dispatch feed. Milbrook Now is not at the scene.

factchecks.claim: The Milbrook Gazette published its final edition in 2014.
factchecks.ruling: The closure date of the Milbrook Gazette is frequently given in local discussion and the figures cited vary. Milbrook Now reviewed the accounts available to us. The Gazette was founded in 1908, published weekly from an office on Front Street in Milbrook, and is not publishing today. Accounts of the closure place it in the middle of the last decade and describe a change in printing arrangements. Taking the available evidence together, and noting that no edition has been published in more than a decade, Milbrook Now rates this claim TRUE. Readers should be aware that some local accounts give a different year.
evidence: The Milbrook Gazette was founded in 1908 and published every Thursday.
The paper's final edition carried a note to readers stating that the stoppage was expected to be temporary.
The paper did not resume publication.
The Gazette's website remains online and carries articles from its final months.
Milbrook has had no newspaper of its own since the closure.
A veterans post in the village began carrying village notices on its website in 2017, the year after the closure.
sources: [url=synth://milbrookgazette.com/]milbrookgazette.com[/url] — the paper's site, no longer updated

factchecks.claim: There is no water main break in Milbrook and no advisory has been issued.
factchecks.ruling: The organisation is correct that the village has not announced a main break and correct that the work described on Front and Second Street is scheduled hydrant flushing. The claim omits that discoloured water was reported on several streets over the same period, that the village of Milbrook publishes no website on which a notice could be checked, and that the organisation's own notice advises residents to run cold taps before doing laundry, which is the advice an advisory would carry. Milbrook Now rates this claim MISSING CONTEXT. The item reporting the advisory remains available and has been updated.
evidence: The organisation's notices page states that there is no advisory and that nothing is wrong with the water.
The same notice advises residents to run the cold tap until it clears before doing laundry.
The village of Milbrook does not maintain a website and did not respond to requests for comment.
The county dashboard lists no advisory for Milbrook and continues to display a notice lifted in 2021.
A subscription newsletter reported that the village clerk's office described the work as routine flushing.
sources: [url=synth://milbrookvfw.org/notices]milbrookvfw.org[/url] — the notices page containing the claim

factchecks.claim: The north end of Verity County was without power for five days after the Gridfall substation fire.
factchecks.ruling: The fire at Gridfall Substation No. 3 in June 2004 took roughly 4,100 customers off the system and some customers were out for five days. Milbrook Now was not able to establish which customers those were, and the utility has never released its internal report. The north end is served through the same tie line and sits at the end of it, which is consistent with a longer restoration. Given the weight of accounts supporting the five-day figure, Milbrook Now rates the claim MOSTLY TRUE. Other accounts of the fire remain in circulation and some of them disagree.
evidence: The fire burned for about six hours and took roughly 4,100 customers off the system.
Some customers were out for five days.
A state utility commission summary published in November 2003 gave the cause as insulation degradation consistent with age.
Verity Valley Power & Light has not released an internal report.
Substation No. 3 was rebuilt in 2015 as an unmanned yard operated remotely.
Video accounts circulating since 2024 give the year, the cause and the death toll inconsistently.

factchecks.claim: The shortwave broadcast heard on County Route 62 began as a prank by a Milbrook teenager.
factchecks.ruling: This explanation is among the most frequently repeated accounts of the broadcast and is the one most often attached to Milbrook. Accounts name an individual, describe equipment said to have been assembled in a garage in the village, and place the beginning of the transmissions in the late 1990s. Milbrook Now was unable to locate a licence, a transmitter or any person willing to be quoted by name. The individual named in those accounts did not respond to a request for comment. Milbrook Now rates the claim UNPROVEN. We note that the broadcast is reported to continue on the same schedule, which several accounts of a prank do not address.
evidence: The broadcast is generally reported on 4.2190 MHz upper sideband at seven minutes past odd hours.
The earliest local documentation is a 1998 thread on a Gridfall message board.
Accounts attaching the broadcast to a Milbrook resident began circulating later.
A county wiki article lists the prank explanation among several that cannot all be correct at once.
No licensed transmitter is listed on the frequency in Verity County.
At least one local logger has published reception data going back to 2019.

corrections.text: An earlier version of this item said a boil notice was in effect in Milbrook. No boil notice has been issued. The reference has been removed. The headline is generated from the item's category and has not been changed.
This item has been updated to include comment from the village of Milbrook. The village did not provide comment.

This item described Route 11 as an express service between Ashkettle and Milbrook. The county transit authority lists no route serving Milbrook and states that Dial-A-Ride is the only public transportation available there. The item has been updated. The headline has not been changed.

An earlier version of this item gave the address of the cited kitchen as 41 Second Street. The address in the county inspection record is 9 Oak Street. Both buildings are veterans halls in Milbrook village and they are separate organisations.

Milbrook Now received four contacts regarding this item. Three were received by telephone at the number in our public notices filing and could not be entered into the corrections queue. One was submitted through the intake form and was actioned.

An earlier version of this item said three people died in the fire at Gridfall Substation No. 3. Nobody was killed. Two Gridfall volunteer firefighters were treated for smoke inhalation at County General and were released the same afternoon. The year and cause given in the item are unchanged.

A reader who identified himself as a retired employee of the utility submitted a correction stating that the fire occurred on 11 June 2003, that the state commission's summary that November gave the cause as insulation degradation consistent with age, and that the summary runs to two pages. The submission did not identify a specific sentence in the item and could not be processed. The reader has submitted eleven requests through the form this year.

A reader in Milbrook wrote to say that the photograph published with this item shows the elementary building at Tessler and not Milbrook Elementary, and that she attended both. The photograph has been replaced with a stock image.
An earlier version of this item referred to the team as Kerrin Consolidated. The team is Kerrin Central.

The correction published on September 15 is withdrawn. Kerrin Consolidated is the school district. Kerrin Central is the school and the team. Both names were correct as they appeared. The correction of October 13 remains posted above for the record.
An earlier version of this item said the Milbrook Gazette employed six people at its close. The figure in our source is four. The year of the closure is unchanged.

A reader wrote to say that the Blue Kestrel reopened eleven days after the kitchen fire of 1977 and operated for a further twenty-nine years. Community Voices columns are the views of the contributor and are not amended at the request of a third party. The column stands as published.

A reader asked whether the Community Voices contributors live in Milbrook. Contributor biographies are supplied by the contributor. Milbrook Now does not verify them and does not publish contributor addresses.

A request was received concerning an obituary in this item, stating that the date of death and the organisation given are both wrong. The item originated at another property in our group and was republished here under our standards document. A request concerning an item that originated at another property must be submitted to that property. The requester was advised of this. The item has not been amended.

A reader wrote through the intake form concerning a notice republished in an obituary roundup, to say that the surname was not hyphenated, that the person was 89 rather than 91, that she lived in Milbrook rather than Marchfield, and that the organisation named in the notice does not exist. The request was acknowledged and assigned reference number 41-2026-8817. No amendment has been made.

A reader asked whether Community Spotlight features are written by our newsroom. They are not. Community Spotlight features are produced with the participating business, which is noted at the foot of each feature and is noted here as well.
An earlier version of this page gave a telephone number for Milbrook Now. The number routes to a group intake queue and is not answered in Milbrook. It has been removed.

This item has been removed at the request of a person named in it. Milbrook Now removes items on request where the subject has supplied documentation. The documentation is not published. Search engines may continue to display the headline for some time.

A librarian in Marchfield wrote in March to ask whether anybody keeps what this site publishes, and whether a copy could be deposited with a library once a year. Items published on this site remain on this site for as long as the property is published. The Group does not deposit copies with a library and has no mechanism for doing so.
